documents.title: IPCC-65: assessment timetable and budget remain unresolved
documents.text: Governments debated when climate assessment reports should be ready for the next global stocktake. The session was suspended without agreement on the assessment timetable or budget. This is a procedural development with consequences for the institution's continuing work, rather than a new scientific finding.
documents.evidence_note: Report content and meeting dates reviewed through web retrieval; original publication date not established. Direct bounded HTTP probe returned 403.

documents.text: The overview says Climate Week 4 was held in Baku in September. Its format joins mandated climate policy meetings with implementation discussions. A calendar and format description alone do not establish particular policy outcomes.

documents.title: Quarterly report describes adaptation and transparency work at Baku Climate Week
documents.text: The secretariat reports that the Baku Adaptation Road Map workshop considered implementation across the adaptation planning and monitoring cycle. At Climate Week, governments and support providers also exchanged practical approaches to transparency reporting. These are substantive implementation discussions; the report does not establish a new negotiated agreement on those points.
documents.evidence_note: The page includes references to reports released on October 27. Its own publication date remains unknown; it cannot be backdated to September.

documents.title: IPCC-65 climate assessment timetable and budget talks suspended
documents.text: The report explains that governments did not agree on the timetable for the next climate assessment or the remaining-cycle budget. Talks were suspended. The timing dispute matters for whether the assessment can inform the next global stocktake, and the unresolved budget has institutional implications.
